notes: Identity assessment: supplied source is a primary accepted author manuscript/post-print of Life History Strategies and Psychopathology: The Faster the Life Strategies, the More Symptoms of Psychopathology, by Jessie E. Hurst and Phillip S. Kavanagh. Its front matter identifies Evolution and Human Behavior, volume 38, issue 1, pp. 1–8 (2017), DOI 10.1016/j.evolhumbehav.2016.06.001, matching the assigned original reference. The supplied text includes methods, results, discussion, references and Tables 1–6; no source PDF was supplied. Only es_value_o is assigned. Target identity remains unresolved because description, study_o and locators_o are blank. Candidate evidence: Table 5 reports age-controlled partial correlations (pr) for Mini-K and HKSS across family structure, psychopathology, self-harm, attachment and aggression; for total psychopathology the printed candidates are -.51 and -.41 respectively. Table 6 reports separate Mini-K and HKSS attachment regressions controlling for age and sibling counts, including attachment beta values -.41 and -.37, model R2 = .28 and .26, and F(5,132) = 10.49 and 9.09, both p < .001. These are different tests, not interchangeable target estimates. Cohen's f^2 is not printed in the inspected results or Tables 5–6; no effect-size conversion was performed. No candidate statistic has been selected by numerical matching. All unassigned fields and the replication side are placeholders only.
